rows: Whether glucose can be tracked continuously in vivo
Amperometric enzymatic CGM
Enzyme drift, lag time, calibration, and biofouling matter.
Whether antigen detection must be fast and cheap
Immunochromatographic lateral flow
Speed trades against sensitivity; sampling quality dominates weak positives.
Whether protein binding kinetics are needed
SPR optical platform such as Biacore
Surface immobilization can change kinetics; mass transport artifacts matter.
Whether pathogen nucleic acid is the target
RT-PCR or CRISPR assay
Amplification is sensitive but contamination and primer specificity are critical.
Whether electrolytes are needed at point of care
Potentiometric ion-selective electrodes
ISEs measure activity, not total concentration, and require calibration.
Whether thin-film mass deposition is the signal
Piezoelectric QCM/QCM-D
Viscosity and viscoelasticity can masquerade as mass.
Whether ambulatory rhythm is the target
ECG electrodes in patches/watches
Consumer devices improve access but still need clinical interpretation.
Whether blood oxygen is the target
PPG pulse oximetry
Motion, perfusion, skin tone, and dyshemoglobins can bias readings.
Whether drug-target affinity is the target
Label-free SPR or LSPR
Affinity without kinetics can mislead; kon/koff often matter clinically.
Whether cell signaling/metabolites need microscale context
Impedimetric or optical lab-on-chip
Microfluidic models simplify physiology and need validation against tissue context.
Whether a pathogen panel needs multiplexing
PCR microfluidics such as FilmArray
Panels detect included targets; they do not rule out organisms outside the assay.
